harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a locked (password-disabled) opsbot account on node1 and node2, generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and verified passwordless key-based SSH from node1's opsbot to node2's opsbot. Confirmed sshd on both nodes enforces PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no for opsbot (and globally). Then performed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on node1 then node2: captured baseline boot_id, triggered async reboot, polled until reconnect, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified sshd active, opsbot account/authorized_keys intact, and cross-node key-based SSH still functional post-restart on both nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline sudo access, OS, and sshd_config on node1 and node2
Created locked opsbot user (useradd -m, passwd -l) on node1 and node2
Generated ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1
Installed opsbot's public key into node2 opsbot's authorized_keys
Verified sshd -T effective config shows PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no for opsbot on both nodes
Verified passwordless key-based SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via async shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id
Verified node1 post-restart: sshd active, opsbot intact, key-based SSH to node2 still works
Restarted node2 via async shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id
Verified node2 post-restart: sshd active, opsbot intact, authorized_keys present
Re-verified end-to-end key-based SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot after both restarts

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd + passwd -l succeeded on both nodes, id opsbot shows uid=1001

evidence.requirement: opsbot has key-based SSH access to run commands on node2
evidence.summary: Generated ed25519 keypair as opsbot on node1, installed pubkey in node2 opsbot authorized_keys, then ssh -o BatchMode=yes from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot succeeded and ran whoami/hostname

evidence.requirement: key-based authentication required (password auth disabled) for opsbot on both systems
evidence.summary: sshd -T -C user=opsbot on both nodes shows pubkeyauthentication yes / passwordauthentication no / kbdinteractiveauthentication no; passwd -S confirms opsbot account is locked (L) with no password on both nodes
Captured boot_id 8336c3a1-... and confirmed sshd active plus opsbot account present pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Async shutdown -r now acknowledged immediately, subsequent poll showed connection refused (node down), later poll returned new boot_id 6fb559c6-... proving a real restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services/data
evidence.summary: sshd active, opsbot account intact, and key-based SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot succeeded after node1's restart
Captured boot_id f19de998-... and confirmed sshd active plus opsbot account present pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Async shutdown -r now acknowledged immediately, subsequent poll showed connection refused (node down), later poll returned new boot_id 400eae5e-... proving a real restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of required services/data and cluster access
evidence.summary: sshd active and opsbot authorized_keys present on node2 after restart; end-to-end key-based SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot re-verified successful with no password prompt
